noun: A word used as the designation or appellation of a creature or thing, existing in fact or in thought; a substantive. Note: By some grammarians the term noun is so used as to include adjectives, as being descriptive; but in general it is limited to substantives.
nonliquet: It is not clear; -- a verdict given by a jury when a matter is to be deferred to another day of trial.
noursle: To nurse; to rear; to bring up. (old) [Written also nosel, nousel, nousle, nowsle, nusle, nuzzle, etc.] She noursled him till years he raught. Spenser.
nonunionist: One who does not belong, or refuses to belong, to a trades union.
noisette: A hybrid rose produced in 1817, by a French gardener, Noisette, of Charleston, South Carolina, from the China rose and the musk rose. It has given rise to many fine varieties, as the Lamarque, the Marechal (or Marshal) Niel, and the Cloth of gold. Most roses of this class have clustered flowers and are of vigorous growth. P. Henderson.
nombles: The entrails of a deer; the umbles. [Written also numbles.] Johnson.
noetic: Of or pertaining to the intellect; intellectual. I would employ the word noetic to express all those cognitions which originate in the mind itself. Sir W. Hamilton.
notebook: 1. A book in which notes or memorandums are written. 2. A book in which notes of hand are registered.
noctilionid: A South American bat of the genus Noctilio, having cheek pouches and large incisor teeth.
noon: No. See the Note under No. (old) | 1. The middle of the day; midday; the time when the sun is in the meridian; twelve o'clock in the daytime. 2. Hence, the highest point; culmination. In the very noon of that brilliant life which was…
notate: Marked with spots or lines, which are often colored. Henslow.
nonylenic: Of, pertaining to, related to, or designating, nonylene or its compounds; as, nonylenic acid.
nonjurorism: The doctrines, or action, of the Nonjurors.
nosel: To nurse; to lead or teach; to foster; to nuzzle. (old) If any man use the Scripture . . . to nosel thee in anything save in Christ, he is a false prophet. Tyndale.
norwegian: Of or pertaining to Norway, its inhabitants, or its language. | 1. A native of Norway. 2. That branch of the Scandinavian language spoken in Norway.
nom: Name. Nom de guerre (, literally, war name; hence, a fictitious name, or one assumed for a time. -- Nom de plume (, literally, pen name; hence, a name assumed by an author as his or her signature.
novaculite: A variety of siliceous slate, of which hones are made; razor stone; Turkey stone; hone stone; whet slate.
noncontent: One who gives a negative vote; -- sometimes abridged into noncon. or non con.
noematical: Of or pertaining to the understanding. (old) Cudworth.
nodation: Act of making a knot, or state of being knotted.
nougat: A cake, sweetmeat, or confectión made with almonds or other nuts.
norna: 1. (Scandinavian Myth.) One of the three Fates, Past, Present, and Future. Their names were Urd, Verdandi, and Skuld. 2. A tutelary deity; a genius.
non: A prefix used in the sense of not; un-; in-; as in nonattention, or non-attention, nonconformity, nonmetallic, nonsuit. Note: The prefix non- may be joined to the leading word by means of a hyphen, or, in most cases, the hyphen may be dispensed with. The list of words having the prefix non- could easily be lengthened.
nonet: A composition for nine instruments, rarely for nine voices.
nonelectric: Not electric; conducting electricity. | A substance that is not an electric; that which transmits electricity, as a metal.
nosology: 1. A systematic arrangement, or classification, of diseases. 2. That branch of medical science which treats of diseases, or of the classification of diseases.
nonylic: Of, pertaining to, or designating, nonyl or its compounds; as, nonylic acid.
notionality: A notional or groundless opinion. Glanvill.
nonmoral: Not moral nor immoral; having no connection with morals; not in the sphere of morals or ethics; not ethical.
nourishable: 1. Capable of being nourished; as, the nourishable parts of the body. Grew. 2. Capable of giving nourishment. (old) Bp. Hall.
nonplane: Not lying in one plane; -- said of certain curves.
nonsexual: Having no distinction of sex; sexless; neuter.
noctivagation: A roving or going about in the night. Gayton.
nosocomial: Of or pertaining to a hospital; as, nosocomial atmosphere. Dunglison.
norroy: The most northern of the English Kings-at-arms. See King-at- arms, under King.
nookshotten: Full of nooks, angles, or corners. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.] That nook-shotten isle of Albion. Shak.
northeaster: A storm, strong wind, or gale, coming from the northeast.
nonmetallic: 1. Not metallic. 2. (Chem.) Resembling, or possessing the properties of, a nonmetal or metalloid; as, sulphur is a nonmetallic element.
nominalism: The principles or philosophy of the Nominalists.
nondecane: A hydrocarbon of the paraffin series, a white waxy substance, C19H40; -- so called from the number of carbon atoms in the molecule.
nodosarine: Resembling in form or structure a foraminiferous shell of the genus Nodosaria. -- n. (Zoöl.) A foraminifer of the genus Nodosaria or of an allied genus.
nonalienation: Failure to alienate; also, the state of not being alienated.
notself: The negative of self. "A cognizance of notself." Sir. W. Hamilton.
novennial: Done or recurring every ninth year.
nowhere: Not anywhere; not in any place or state; as, the book is nowhere to be found.
northerly: Of or pertaining to the north; toward the north, or from the north; northern.
novelty: 1. The quality or state of being novel; newness; freshness; recentness of origin or introduction. Novelty is the great parent of pleasure. South. 2. Something novel; a new or strange thing.
nova: A new star, usually appearing suddenly, shining for a brief period, and then sinking into obscurity. Such appearances are supposed to result from cosmic collisions, as of a dark star with interstellar nebulosities. The most important modern novæ are: -- No"va Co*ro"næ Bo`re*a"lis [1866]; No"va Cyg"ni [1876]; No"va An*dro"me*dæ [1885]; No"va Au*ri"gæ [1891-92];
nonsubmission: Want of submission; failure or refusal to submit.
notch: 1. A hollow cut in anything; a nick; an indentation. And on the stick ten equal notches makes. Swift. 2. A narrow passage between two elevation; a deep, close pass; a defile; | 1. To cut or make notches in ; to indent; also, to score by notches; as, to notch a stick. 2. To fit the notch of (an arrow) to the string. God is all sufferance;
noctidial: Comprising a night and a day; a noctidial day. Holder.
noonday: Midday; twelve o'clock in the day; noon. | Of or pertaining to midday; meridional; as, the noonday heat. "Noonday walks." Addison.
nomadic: Of or pertaining to nomads, or their way of life; wandering; moving from place to place for subsistence; as, a nomadic tribe. -- No*mad"ic*al*ly, adv.
nonsonant: Not sonant. -- n. A nonsonant or nonvocal consonant.
nowthe: Just now; at present. (old) But thereof needeth not to speak as nouthe. Chaucer.
novitiate: 1. The state of being a novice; time of initiation or instruction in rudiments. 2. Hence: Time of probation in a religious house before taking the vows. 3. One who is going through a novitiate, or period of probation; a novice. Addison. 4. The place where novices live or are trained.
nonstriated: Without striations; unstriped; as, nonstriated muscle fibers.
noninhabitant: One who is not an inhabitant; a stranger; a foreigner; a nonresident.
nodulose: Having small nodes or knots; diminutively nodose.
novilunar: Of or pertaining to the new moon.
noncondensing: Not condensing; discharging the steam from the cylinder at a pressure nearly equal to or above that of the atmosphere and not into a condenser.
notify: 1. To make known; to declare; to publish; as, to notify a fact to a person. No law can bind till it be notified or promulged. Sowth. 2. To give notice to; to inform by notice; to apprise; as, the constable has notified the citizens to meet at the city hall; the bell notifies us of the time of meeting.
nonagrian: Any moth of the genus Nonagria and allied genera, as the spindleworm and stalk borer.
nodosity: 1. The quality of being knotty or nodose; resemblance to a node or swelling; knottiness. Holland. 2. A knot; a node.
nosesmart: A kind of cress, a pungent cruciferous plant, including several species of the genus Nasturtium.
nonestinventus: The return of a sheriff on a writ, when the defendant is not found in his county. Bouvier.
nominalistic: Of or pertaining to the Nominalists.
notionist: One whose opinions are ungrounded notions. Bp. Hopkins.
november: The eleventh month of the year, containing thirty days.
nomocracy: Government in accordance with a system of law. Milman.
nominative: Giving a name; naming; designating; -- said of that case or form of a noun which stands as the subject of a finite verb. -- n. The nominative case.
norse: Of or pertaining to ancient Scandinavia, or to the language spoken by its inhabitants.
nodulous: Having small nodes or knots; diminutively nodose.
northward: Toward the north; nearer to the north than to the east or west point. | Toward the north, or toward a point nearer to the north than to the east or west point.
nonmetal: Any one of the set of elements which, as contrasted with the metals, possess, produce, or receive, acid rather than basic properties; a metalloid; as, oxygen, sulphur, and chlorine are nonmetals.
nominal: 1. Of or pertaining to a name or names; having to do with the literal meaning of a word; verbal; as, a nominal definition. Bp. Pearson. 2. Existing in name only; not real; as, a nominal difference. | 1. A nominalist. (old) Camden. 2. (Gram.) A verb formed from a noun. 3. A name; an appellation. A is the nominal of the sixth note in the natural diatonic scale. Moore (Encyc. of Music. )
noematic: Of or pertaining to the understanding. (old) Cudworth.
noddle: 1. The head; -- used jocosely or contemptuously. Come, master, I have a project in my noddle. L'Estrange. 2. The back part of the head or neck. (old) For occasion ... turneth a bald noddle, after she hath presented her locks in front, and no hold taken. Bacon.
notodontian: Any one of several species of bombycid moths belonging to Notodonta, Nerice, and allied genera. The caterpillar of these moths has a hump, or spine, on its back.
nothing: 1. Not anything; no thing (in the widest sense of the word thing); -- opposed to Ant: anything and Ant: something. Yet had his aspect nothing of severe. Dryden. 2. Nonexistence; nonentity; | In no degree; not at all; in no wise. Adam, with such counsel nothing swayed. Milton. The influence of reason in producing our passions is nothing near so extensive as is commonly believed. Burke.
normalization: Reduction to a standard or normal state.
nomad: One of a race or tribe that has no fixed location, but wanders from place to place in search of pasture or game.
noonflower: The goat's beard, whose flowers close at midday.
notability: 1. Quality of being notable. 2. A notable, or remarkable, person or thing; a person of note. "Parisian notabilities" Carlyle. 3. A notable saying. (old) Chaucer.
nonepiscopal: Not Episcopal; not pertaining to the Episcopal church or system.
nosegay: A bunch of odorous and showy flowers; a bouquet; a posy. Pope.
noctiluca: 1. (Old Chem.) That which shines at night; -- a fanciful name for phosphorus. 2. (Zoöl.) A genus of marine flagellate Infusoria, remarkable for their unusually large size and complex structure, as well as for their phosphorescence. The brilliant diffuse phosphorescence of the sea is often due to myriads of Noctilucæ.
nonconduction: The quality of not being able to conduct or transmit; failure to conduct.
notation: 1. The act or practice of recording anything by marks, figures, or characters. 2. Any particular system of characters, symbols, or abbreviated expressions used in art or science, to express briefly technical facts, quantities, etc. Esp., the system of figures, letters, and signs used in arithmetic and algebra to express number, quantity, or operations. 3.
notelet: A little or short note; a billet.
noticeable: Capable of being observed; worthy of notice; likely to attract observation; conspicous. A noticeable man, with large gray eyes. Wordsworth.
nobleminded: Having a noble mind; honorable; magnanimous. -- No"ble-mind`ed*ness, n.
noblewoman: A female of noble rank; a peeress.
norian: Pertaining to the upper portion of the Laurentian rocks. T. S. Hunt.
nonobedience: Neglect of obedience; failure to obey.
notwithstanding: Without prevention, or obstruction from or by; in spite of. We gentil women bee Loth to displease any wight, Notwithstanding our great right. Chaucer's Dream. Those on whom Christ bestowed miraculous… | Nevertheless; however; although; as, I shall go, notwithstanding it rains. I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant. Notwithstanding, in thy days I will not do it.
nonattendance: A failure to attend; omission of attendance; nonappearance.
noule: The top of the head; the head or noll. (old) Spenser.
nould: Would not. (old) "By those who nould repent." Fairfax.
nodical: Of or pertaining to the nodes; from a node to the same node again; as, the nodical revolutions of the moon. Nodical month. See Lunar month, under Month.
nourisher: One who, or that which, nourishes. Milton.
noctilucin: A fatlike substance in certain marine animals, to which they owe their phosphorescent properties.
nonruminant: Not ruminating; as, a nonruminant animal.
nonacquaintance: Want of acquaintance; the state of being unacquainted.
nobleman: One of the nobility; a noble; a peer; one who enjoys rank above a commoner, either by virtue of birth, by office, or by patent.
nomancy: The art or practice of divining the destiny of persons by the letters which form their names. NO-MAN'S LAND No"-man's` land`. 1. (Naut.) A space amidships used to keep blocks, ropes, etc.; a space on a ship belonging to no one in particular to care for. 2. Fig.: An unclaimed space or time. That no-man's land of twilight. W. Black.
noisiness: The state or quality of being noisy.
nonprofessional: Not belonging to a profession; not done by, or proceeding from, professional men; contrary to professional usage.
nonregardance: Want of due regard; disregard; slight. (old) Shak.
northmost: Lying farthest north; northernmost. Northmost part of the coast of Mozambique. De Foe.
nonylene: Any one of a series of metameric, unsaturated hydrocarbons C9H18 of the ethylene series.
nod: 1. To bend or incline the upper part, with a quick motion; as, nodding plumes. 2. To incline the head with a quick motion; to make a slight bow; to make a motion of assent, of salutation, or of… | 1. To incline or bend, as the head or top; to make a motion of assent, of salutation, or of drowsiness with; as, to nod the head. 2. To signify by a nod; as, to nod approbation. 3. To cause to bend.
nonetto: A composition for nine instruments, rarely for nine voices.
nonpreparation: Neglect or failure to prepare; want of preparation.
northumbrian: Of or pertaining to Northumberland in England. -- n. A native or inhabitant of Northumberland.
nonessential: Not essential. | A thing not essential.
nonpareil: 1. Something of unequaled excellence; a peerless thing or person; a nonesuch; -- often used as a name. 2. Etym: [F. nonpareille.] (Print.) A size of type next smaller than minion and next larger than agate (or ruby). Note: This line is printed in the type called nonpareil. 3. (Zoöl.) (a) A beautifully colored finch (Passerina ciris), native of the Southern United States.
nonimportation: Want or failure of importation; a not importing of commodities.
nondelivery: A neglect or failure of delivery; omission of delivery.
norfolkdumpling: (a) A kind of boiled dumpling made in Norfolk. (b) A native or inhabitant of Norfolk.
noxious: 1. Hurtful; harmful; baneful; pernicious; injurious; destructive; unwholesome; insalubrious; as, noxious air, food, or climate; pernicious; corrupting to morals; as, noxious practices or examples. Too frequent an appearance in places of public resort is noxious to spiritual promotions. Swift. 2. Guilty; criminal. Those who are noxious in the eye of the law. Abp. Bramhall. Syn.
nottheaded: Having the hair cut close. (old) Chapman.
noiseless: Making, or causing, no noise or bustle; without noise; silent; as, the noiseless foot of time. So noiseless would I live. Dryden. -- Noise"less*ly, adv. -- Noise"less*ness, n.
nonunion: 1. Not belonging to, or affiliated with, a trades union; as, a nonunoin carpenter. 2. Not recognizing or favoring trades unions or trades-unionists; as, a nonunion contractor. --Non*un"ion*ism (#), n.
nowise: Not in any manner or degree; in no way; noways. Others whose case is nowise different. Earle.
notching: 1. The act of making notches; the act of cutting into small hollows. 2. The small hollow, or hollows, cut; a notch or notches. 3. (Carp.) A method of joining timbers, scantling, etc., by notching them, as at the ends, and overlapping or interlocking the notched portions. 4. (Engin.) A method of excavating, as in a bank, by a series of cuttings side by side. See also Gulleting.
nonestfactum: The plea of the general issue in an action of debt on bond.
nonprosequitur: A judgment entered against the plaintiff in a suit where he does not appear to prosecute. See Nolle prosequi.
nonsense: 1. That which is not sense, or has no sense; words, or language, which have no meaning, or which convey no intelligible ideas; absurdity. 2. Trifles; things of no importance.
nonsensical: Without sense; unmeaning; absurb; foolish; irrational; preposterous. -- Non*sen"si*cal*ly, adv. -- Non*sen"si*cal*ness, n.
nondo: A coarse umbelliferous plant (Ligusticum actæifolium) with a large aromatic root. It is found chiefly in the Alleghany region. Also called Angelico.
nosophen: An iodine compound obtained as a yellowish gray, odorless, tasteless powder by the action of iodine on phenolphthalein.
nototrema: The pouched, or marsupial, frog of South America.
nonage: The ninth part of movable goods, formerly payable to the clergy on the death of persons in their parishes. Mozley & W. | Time of life before a person becomes of age; legal immaturity; minority. The human mind . . . was still in its nonage. Coleridge.
nonassumpsit: The general plea or denial in an action of assumpsit.
notice: 1. The act of noting, remarking, or observing; observation by the senses or intellect; cognizance; note. How ready is envy to mingle with the notices we take of other persons ! I. Watts. 2. | 1. To observe; to see to mark; to take note of; to heed; to pay attention to. 2. To show that one has observed; to take public note of; remark upon; to make comments on; to refer to;
nonchalantly: In a nonchalant, indifferent, or careless manner; coolly.
nowel: 1. Christmas; also, a shout of joy at Christmas for the birth of the Savior. (old) 2. (Mus.) A kind of hymn, or canticle, of mediæval origin, sung in honor of the Nativity of our Lord; | (a) The core, or the inner part, of a mold for casting a large hollow object. (b) The bottom part of a mold or of a flask, in distinction from the cope; the drag.
norm: 1. A rule or authoritative standard; a model; a type. 2. (Biol.) A typical, structural unit; a type. Agassiz.
nosebleed: 1. A bleeding at the nose. 2. (Bot.) The yarrow. See Yarrow.
notandum: A thing to be noted or observed; a notable fact; -- chiefly used in the plural.
notary: 1. One who records in shorthand what is said or done; as, the notary of an ecclesiastical body. 2. (Eng. & Am. Law) A public officer who attests or certifies deeds and other writings, or copies of them, usually under his official seal, to make them authentic, especially in foreign countries.
normalcy: The quality, state, or fact of being normal; as, the point of normalcy.
nombril: A point halfway between the fess point and the middle base point of an escutcheon; -- called also navel point. See Escutcheon.
norfolkjacket: A kind of loose-fitting plaited jacket, having a loose belt.
novenary: Of or pertaining to the number nine. | The number of nine units; nine, collectively.
nourishment: 1. The act of nourishing, or the state of being nourished; nutrition. 2. That which serves to nourish; nutriment; food. Learn to seek the nourishment of their souls. Hooker.
nooning: A rest at noon; a repast at noon.
nonpros: To decline or fail to prosecute; to allow to be dropped (said of a suit); to enter judgment against (a plaintiff who fails to prosecute); as, the plaintiff was non-prossed.
nowed: Knotted; tied in a knot, as a serpent.
nonappearance: Default of apperance, as in court, to prosecute or defend; failure to appear.
nolleity: The state of being unwilling; nolition.
notobranchiate: Of or pertaining to the Notobranchiata.
nomothetical: Legislative; enacting laws; as, a nomothetical power. Bp. Barlow.
nobly: 1. Of noble extraction; as, nobly born or descended. 2. In a noble manner; with greatness of soul; heroically; with magnanimity; as, a deed nobly done. 3. Splendidly; magnificently. Syn. -- Illustriously; honorably; magnanimously; heroically; worthly; eminently; grandly.
noah: A patriarch of Biblical history, in the time of the Deluge. Noah's ark. (a) (Zoöl.) A marine bivalve shell (Arca Noæ), which somewhat resembles an ark, or ship, in form. (b) A child's toy, consisting of an ark-shaped box containing many different wooden animals.
nonentity: 1. Nonexistence; the negation of being. 2. A thing not existing. South. 3. A person or thing of little or no account. [Colloq.]
noematachograph: An instrument for determining and registering the duration of more or less complex operations of the mind. Dunglison.
nobelprizes: Prizes for the encouragement of men and women who work for the interests of humanity, established by the will of A. B. Nobel (1833- 96), the Swedish inventor of dynamite, who left his entire estate for this purpose.
nonelect: A person or persons not elected, or chosen, to salvation.
nonaged: Having the quality of nonage; being a minor; immature. W. Browne.
northeast: The point between the north and east, at an equal distance from each; the northeast part or region. | Of or pertaining to the northeast; proceeding toward the northeast, or coming from that point; as, a northeast course; a northeast wind. Northeast passage, a passage or communication by sea between…
noncondensible: Not condensible; incapable of being liquefied; -- said of gases.
norlander: A northener; a person from the north country.
nounize: To change (an adjective, verb, etc.) into a noun. Earle.
noncompos: Not of sound mind; not having the regular use of reason; hence, also, as a noun, an idiot; a lunati NONCON. Non"con. (, n. See Noncontent.
nondeposition: A failure to deposit or throw down.
nome: 1. A province or political division, as of modern Greece or ancient Egypt; a nomarchy. 2. Any melody determined by inviolable rules. (old)
nodal: Of the nature of, or relating to, a node; as, a nodal point. Nodal line, Nodal point, in a vibrating plate or cord, that line or point which remains at rest while the other parts of the body are in a state of vibration.
northwards: Toward the north, or toward a point nearer to the north than to the east or west point.
nonobstante: 1. Notwithstanding; in opposition to, or in spite of, what has been stated, or is to be stated or admitted. 2. (Law) A clause in old English statutes and letters patent, importing a license from the crown to do a thing notwithstanding any statute to the contrary. This dispensing power was abolished by the Bill of Rights.
nostril: 1. (Anat.) One of the external openings of the nose, which give passage to the air breathed and to secretions from the nose and eyes; one of the anterior nares. Note: In sperm whales, porpoises, and allied animals, there is only one nostril, which is situated on the top of the head and called a spiracle. 2. Perception; insight; acuteness.
norium: A supposed metal alleged to have been discovered in zircon.
nonda: The edible plumlike fruit of the Australian tree, Parinarium Nonda.
nomic: Customary; ordinary; -- applied to the usual English spelling, in distinction from strictly phonetic methods. H Sweet. -- n. Nomic spelling. A. J. Ellis.
nonagon: A figure or polygon having nine sides and nine angles.
nominalist: One of a sect of philosophers in the Middle Ages, who adopted the opinion of Roscelin, that general conceptions, or universals, exist in name only. Reid.
nopal: A cactaceous plant (Nopalea cochinellifera), originally Mexican, on which the cochineal insect feeds, and from which it is collected. The name is sometimes given to other species of Cactaceæ.
noways: In no manner or degree; not at all; nowise. But Ireland will noways allow that name unto it. Fuller.
nobleness: The quality or state of being noble; greatness; dignity; magnanimity; elevation of mind, character, or station; nobility; grandeur; stateliness. His purposes are full honesty, nobleness, and integrity. Jer. Taylor.
nolpros: To discontinue by entering a nolle prosequi; to decline to prosecute.
norland: 1. The land in the north; north country. [Chiefly Poetic] 2. = Norlander. [Scot. & Eng.]
nonmember: One who is not a member.
nonyl: The hydrocarbon radical, C9H19, derived from nonane and forming many compounds. Used also adjectively; as, nonyl alcohol.
nonobservance: Neglect or failure to observe or fulfill.
nomarchy: A province or territorial division of a kingdom, under the rule of a nomarch, as in modern Greece; a nome.
noctuary: A record of what passes in the night; a nightly journal; -- distinguished from diary. Addison.
nonmedullated: Not medullated; (Anat.) without a medulla or marrow, or without a medullary sheath; as, a nonmedullated nerve fiber.
norwegium: A rare metallic element, of doubtful identification, said to occur in the copper-nickel of Norway.
noisome: 1. Noxious to health; hurtful; mischievous; unwholesome; insalubrious; destructive; as, noisome effluvia. "Noisome pestilence." Ps. xci. 3. 2. Offensive to the smell or other senses; disgusting; fetid. "Foul breath is noisome." Shak. -- Noi"some*ly, adv. -- Noi"some*ness, n. Syn. -- Noxious; unwholesome; insalubrious; mischievous; destructive. -- Noisome, Noxious.
norite: A granular crystalline rock consisting essentially of a triclinic feldspar (as labradorite) and hypersthene.
nonconductor: A substance which does not conduct, that is, convey or transmit, heat, electricity, sound, vibration, or the like, or which transmits them with difficulty; an insulator; as, wool is a nonconductor of heat; glass and dry wood are nonconductors of electricity.
northerner: 1. One born or living in the north. 2. A native or inhabitant of the Northern States; -- contradistinguished from Ant: Southerner. [U. S.]
nosography: A description or classification of diseases.
novelist: 1. An innovator; an asserter of novelty. (old) Cudworth. 2. Etym: [Cf. F. nouvelliste, It. novellista.] A writer of news. (old) Tatler (178). 3. Etym: [Cf. F. nouvelliste.] A writer of a novel or novels.
noteless: Not attracting notice; not conspicuous. Noteless as the race from which he sprung. Sir W. Scott.
northwester: A storm or gale from the northwest; a strong northwest wind.
noumenal: Of or pertaining to the noumenon; real; -- opposed to phenomenal. G. H. Lewes.
nonaerobiotic: Capable of living without atmospheric oxygen; anaërobiotic.
noetian: One of the followers of Noetus, who lived in the third century. He denied the distinct personality of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.
noropianic: Of, pertaining to, or designating, an acid of the aromatic series obtained from opianic acid.
nob: A person in a superior position in life; a nobleman. [Slang]
noachian: Of or pertaining to the patriarch Noah, or to his time.
nonoic: Pertaining to, derived from, or resembling, nonane; as, nonoic acid, which is also called pelargonic acid. Cf. Pelargonic.
nonphotobiotic: Capable of living without light; as, nonphotobiotic plant cells, or cells which habitually live in darkness.
notidanian: Any one of several species of sharks of the family Notidanidæ, or Hexanchidæ. Called also cow sharks. See Shark.
noncompletion: Lack of completion; failure to complete.
noctuid: Any one of numerous moths of the family Noctuidæ, or Noctuælitæ, as the cutworm moths, and armyworm moths; -- so called because they fly at night. -- a. Of or pertaining to the noctuids, or family Noctuidæ.
nobilify: To make noble; to nobiliate. (old) NOBILI'S RINGS No"bi*li's rings. [After Leopoldo Nobili, an Italian physicist who first described them in 1826.] (Physics) Colored rings formed upon a metal plate by the electrolytic disposition of copper, lead peroxide, etc. They may be produced by touching with a pointed zinc rod a silver plate on which is a solution of copper sulphate.
nonacceptance: A neglect or refusal to accept.
notarial: Of or pertaining to a notary; done or taken by a notary; as, a notarial seal; notarial evidence or attestation.
nominee: A person named, or designated, by another, to any office, duty, or position; one nominated, or proposed, by others for office or for election to office.
northerliness: The quality or state of being northerly; direction toward the north.
nonmembership: State of not being a member.
nomadize: To lead the life of a nomad; to wander with flocks and herds for the sake of finding pasturage. The Vogules nomadize chiefly about the Rivers Irtish, Obi, Kama, and Volga. W. Tooke.
nothingness: 1. Nihility; nonexistence. 2. The state of being of no value; a thing of no value.
nonconstat: It does not appear; it is not plain or clear; it does not follow.
nobless: 1. Dignity; greatness; noble birth or condition. (old) Chaucer. Spenser. B. Jonson. 2. The nobility; persons of noble rank collectively, including males and females. Dryden.
notochord: An elastic cartilagelike rod which is developed beneath the medullary groove in the vertebrate embryo, and constitutes the primitive axial skeleton around which the centra of the vertebræ and the posterior part of the base of the skull are developed; the chorda dorsalis. See Illust. of Ectoderm.
nolimetangere: 1. (Bot.) (a) Any plant of a genus of herbs (Impatiens) having capsules which, if touched when ripe, discharge their seeds. -- See Impatiens. (b) The squirting cucumber. See under Cucumber. 2. (Med.) A name formerly applied to several varieties of ulcerous cutaneous diseases, but now restricted to Lupus exedens, an ulcerative affection of the nose.
novelize: 1. To innovate. (old) 2. To put into the form of novels; to represent by fiction. "To novelize history." Sir J. Herschel.
notion: 1. Mental apprehension of whatever may be known or imagined; an idea; a conception; more properly, a general or universal conception, as distinguishable or definable by marks or notæ. What hath been generally agreed on, I content myself to assume under the notion of principles. Sir I. Newton. Few agree in their notions about these words. Cheyne.
nonsensitive: Not sensitive; wanting sense or perception; not easily affected.
nonillion: According to the French and American notation, a thousand octillions, or a unit with thirty ciphers annexed; according to the English notation, a million octillions, or a unit with fifty-four ciphers annexed. See the Note under Numeration.
nonnecessity: Absence of necessity; the quality or state of being unnecessary.
nowhither: Not anywhither; in no direction; nowhere. (old) "Thy servant went nowhither." 2 Kings v. 25.
nonacid: Destitute of acid properties; hence, basic; metallic; positive; -- said of certain atoms and radicals.
nodder: One who nods; a drowsy person.
nolleprosequi: Will not prosecute; -- an entry on the record, denoting that a plaintiff discontinues his suit, or the attorney for the public a prosecution; either wholly, or as to some count, or as to some of several defendants.
nook: A narrow place formed by an angle in bodies or between bodies; a corner; a recess; a secluded retreat. How couldst thou find this dark, sequestered nook Milton.
norman: A wooden bar, or iron pin. W. C. Russell. | Of or pertaining to Normandy or to the Normans; as, the Norman language; the Norman conquest. Norman style (Arch.), a style of architecture which arose in the tenth century, characterized by great…
nonconforming: Not conforming; declining conformity; especially, not conforming to the established church of a country.
nonresident: Not residing in a particular place, on one's own estate, or in one's proper place; as, a nonresident clergyman or proprietor of lands. | A nonresident person; one who does not reside in the State or jurisdiction.
nodated: Knotted. Nodated hyperbola (Geom.), a certain curve of the third order having two branches which cross each other, forming a node.
nonsuit: A neglect or failure by the plaintiff to follow up his suit; a stopping of the suit; a renunciation or withdrawal of the cause by the plaintiff, either because he is satisfied that he can not support… | To determine, adjudge, or record (a plaintiff) as having dropped his suit, upon his withdrawal or failure to follow it up. "When two are joined in a writ, and one is nonsuited." Z. Swift.
nones: 1. (Roman Cal.) The fifth day of the months January, February, April, June, August, September, November, and December, and the seventh day of March, May, July, and October. The nones were nine days before the ides, reckoning inclusively, according to the Roman method. 2. Etym: [F. none, fr. L.
nonregent: A master of arts whose regency has ceased. See Regent.
nomothetic: Legislative; enacting laws; as, a nomothetical power. Bp. Barlow.
nobility: 1. The quality or state of being noble; superiority of mind or of character; commanding excellence; eminence. Though she hated Amphialus, yet the nobility of her courage prevailed over it. Sir P. Sidney. They thought it great their sovereign to control, And named their pride nobility of soul. Dryden. 2. The state of being of high rank or noble birth; patrician dignity;
noncontagious: Not contagious; not catching; not communicable by contact. -- Non`con*ta"gious*ness, n.
nodule: A rounded mass or irregular shape; a little knot or lump.
nonjuror: One of those adherents of James II. who refused to take the oath of allegiance to William and Mary, or to their successors, after the revolution of 1688; a Jacobite.
none: 1. No one; not one; not anything; -- frequently used also partitively, or as a plural, not any. There is none that doeth good; no, not one. Ps. xiv. 3. Six days ye shall gather it, but on the seventh day, which is the Sabbath, in it there shall be none. Ex. xvi. 26. Terms of peace yet none Vouchsafed or sought. Milton. None of their productions are extant. Blair. 2. No;
nopalry: A plantation of the nopal for raising the cochineal insect.
nonproficiency: Want of proficiency; failure to make progress.
nodular: Of, pertaining to, or in the form of, a nodule or knot.
nonclaim: A failure to make claim within the time limited by law; omission of claim.
notal: Of or pertaining to the back; dorsal.
notable: 1. Capable of being noted; noticeable; plan; evident. 2. Worthy of notice; remarkable; memorable; noted or distinguished; as, a notable event, person. Note: Notable in the sense of careful, thrifty,… | 1. A person, or thing, of distinction. 2. (French Hist.) One of a number of persons, before the revolution of 1789, chiefly of the higher orders, appointed by the king to constitute a representative…
nor: A negative connective or particle, introducing the second member or clause of a negative proposition, following neither, or not, in the first member or clause (as or in affirmative propositions follows either). Nor is also used sometimes in the first member for neither, and sometimes the neither is omitted and implied by the use of nor.
nonvocal: Not vocal; destitute of tone. -- n. A nonvocal consonant.
nonjoinder: The omission of some person who ought to have been made a plaintiff or defendant in a suit, or of some cause of action which ought to be joined.
nodose: 1. Knotty; having numerous or conspicuous nodes. 2. (Zoöl.) Having nodes or prominences; having the alternate joints enlarged, as the antennæ of certain insects.
nobley: 1. The body of nobles; the nobility. (old) Chaucer. 2. Noble birth; nobility; dignity. (old) Chaucer.
noneffective: 1. Not effective. 2. (Mil.) Not fit or available for duty.
nourish: 1. To feed and cause to grow; to supply with matter which increases bulk or supplies waste, and promotes health; to furnish with nutriment. He planteth an ash, and the rain doth nourish it. Is. xliv. | 1. To promote growth; to furnish nutriment. Grains and roots nourish more than their leaves. Bacon. 2. To gain nourishment. Bacon.
novene: Relating to, or dependent on, the number nine; novenary. The triple and novene division ran throughout. Milman.
nototherium: An extinct genus of gigantic herbivorous marsupials, found in the Pliocene formation of Australia.
noncombatant: Any person connected with an army, or within the lines of an army, who does not make it his business to fight, as any one of the medical officers and their assistants, chaplains, and others; also, any of the citizens of a place occupied by an army; also, any one holding a similar position with respect to the navy.
noose: A running knot, or loop, which binds the closer the more it is drawn. | To tie in a noose; to catch in a noose; to entrap; to insnare.
noter: 1. One who takes notice. 2. An annotator. (old)
nonterm: A vacation between two terms of a court.
nonrendition: Neglect of rendition; the not rendering what is due. The nonrendition of a service which is due. S. E. Dwight.
nobby: Stylish; modish; elegant; showy; aristocratic; fashionable. [Slang]
noumenon: The of itself unknown and unknowable rational object, or thing in itself, which is distinguished from the Ant: phenomenon through which it is apprehended by the senses, and by which it is interpreted and understood; -- so used in the philosophy of Kant and his followers.
nondeciduate: Characterized by the absence of a decidua; indeciduate.
nontenure: A plea of a defendant that he did not hold the land, as affirmed.
northern: 1. Of or pertaining to the north; being in the north, or nearer to that point than to the east or west. 2. In a direction toward the north; as, to steer a northern course; coming from the north; as, a northern wind. Northern diver. (Zoöl.) See Loon. -- Northern lights. See Aurora borealis, under Aurora.
nonego: The union of being and relation as distinguished from, and contrasted with, the ego. See Ego.
novation: 1. Innovation. (old) I shall easily grant that novations in religion are a main cause of distempers in commonwealths. Laud. 2. (Law) A substitution of a new debt for an old one; also, the remodeling of an old obligation.
nocturnal: 1. Of, pertaining to, done or occuring in, the night; as, nocturnal darkness, cries, expedition, etc.; -- opposed to Ant: diurnal. Dryden. 2. Having a habit of seeking food or moving about at night; | An instrument formerly used for taking the altitude of the stars, etc., at sea. I. Watts.
nonpresentation: Neglect or failure to present; state of not being presented.
nonuniformist: One who believes that past changes in the structure of the earth have proceeded from cataclysms or causes more violent than are now operating; -- called also nonuniformitarian.
notobranchiata: (a) A division of nudibranchiate mollusks having gills upon the back. (b) The Dorsibranchiata.
noemics: The science of the understanding; intellectual science.
noteworthy: Worthy of observation or notice; remarkable.
north: 1. That one of the four cardinal points of the compass, at any place, which lies in the direction of the true meridian, and to the left hand of a person facing the east; | Lying toward the north; situated at the north, or in a northern direction from the point of observation or reckoning; proceeding toward the north, or coming from the north. North following.
nomadism: The state of being a nomad.
nowd: The European gray gurnard (Trigla gurnardus). [Written also knoud.]
nolocontendere: A plea, by the defendant, in a criminal prosecution, which, without admitting guilt, subjects him to all the consequences of a plea of quilty. NOL. PROS.; NOL PROS Nol. pros. An abbrev. of Nolle prosequi.
northness: A tendency in the end of a magnetic needle to point to the north. Faraday.
nonusance: Neglect of using; failure to use. Sir T. Browne.
noseband: That part of the headstall of a bridle which passes over a horse's nose.
notification: 1. The act of notifying, or giving notice; the act of making known; especially, the act of giving official notice or information to the public or to individuals, corporations, companies, or societies, by words, by writing, or by other means. 2. Notice given in words or writing, or by signs. 3. The writing which communicates information; an advertisement, or citation, etc.
nonjuring: Not swearing allegiance; -- applied to the party in Great Britain that would not swear allegiance to William and Mary, or their successors.
nonvernacular: Not vernacular. A nonvernacular expression. Sir W. Hamilton.
northeasterly: Pertaining to the northeast; toward the northeast, or coming from the northeast.
noyau: A cordial of brandy, etc., flavored with the kernel of the bitter almond, or of the peach stone, etc.
nonplus: A state or condition which daffles reason or confounds judgment; insuperable difficalty; inability to proceed or decide; puzzle; quandary. Both of them are a perfect nonplus and baffle to all human… | To puzzle; to confound; to perplex; to cause to stop by embarrassment. He has been nonplused by Mr. Dry's desiring him to tell what it was that he endeavored to prove. Spectator.
notornis: A genus of birds allied to the gallinules, but having rudimentary wings and incapable of flight. Notornis Mantelli was first known as a fossil bird of New Zealand, but subsequently a few individuals were found living on the southern island. It is supposed to be now nearly or quite extinct.
nonesuch: A person or thing of a sort that there is no other such; something extraordinary; a thing that has not its equal. It is given as a name to various objects, as to a choice variety of apple, a species of medic (Medicago lupulina), a variety of pottery clay, etc.
nonextensile: Not extensile; incapable of being stretched.
nobiliary: Of or pertaining to the nobility. Fitzed. Hall.
nosebag: A bag in which feed for a horse, ox, or the like, may be fastened under the nose by a string passing over the head.
novercal: Done or recurring every ninth year. | Of or pertaining to a stepmother; suitable to, or in the manner of, a stepmother. Derham.
nonlimitation: Want of limitation; failure to limit.
normal: 1. According to an established norm, rule, or principle; conformed to a type, standard, or regular form; performing the proper functions; not abnormal; regular; natural; analogical. | 1. (Geom.) Any perpendicular. 2. (Geom.) A straight line or plane drawn from any point of a curve or surface so as to be perpendicular to the curve or surface at that point.
nonproduction: A failure to produce or exhibit.
nonone: Any one of several metameric unsaturated hydrocarbons (C9H14) of the valylene series.
nock: 1. A notch. He took his arrow by the nock. Chapman. 2. (Naut.) The upper fore corner of a boom sail or of a trysail. | To notch; to fit to the string, as an arrow; to string, as a bow. Chapman.
noway: In no manner or degree; not at all; nowise. But Ireland will noways allow that name unto it. Fuller.
nose: 1. (Anat.) The prominent part of the face or anterior extremity of the head containing the nostrils and olfactory cavities; the olfactory organ. See Nostril, and Olfactory organ under Olfactory. 2. | 1. To smell; to scent; hence, to track, or trace out. 2. To touch with the nose; to push the nose into or against; hence, to interfere with; to treat insolently. Lambs . . .
nomography: A treatise on laws; an exposition of the form proper for laws.
noctule: A large European bat (Vespertilio, or Noctulina, altivolans).
notchweed: A foul-smelling weed, the stinking goosefoot (Chenopodium Vulvaria).
nobilitation: The act of making noble. (old) Dr. H. More.
northwestern: Of, pertaining to, or being in, the northwest; in a direction toward the northwest; coming from the northwest; northwesterly; as, a northwestern course.
noble: 1. Possessing eminence, elevation, dignity, etc.; above whatever is low, mean, degrading, or dishonorable; magnanimous; as, a noble nature or action; a noble heart. | 1. A person of rank above a commoner; a nobleman; a peer. 2. An English money of account, and, formerly, a gold coin, of the value of 6 s. 8 d. sterling, or about $1.61. 3. (Zoöl.) A European fish;
nonconducting: Not conducting; not transmitting a fluid or force; thus, in electricity, wax is a nonconducting substance.
novatianism: The doctrines or principles of the Novatians. Milner.
noise: 1. Sound of any kind. The heavens turn about in a most rapid motion without noise to us perceived. Bacon. Note: Noise is either a sound of too short a duration to be determined, like the report of a… | To sound; to make a noise. Milton.
no: Not any; not one; none. Let there be no strife ... between me and thee. Gen. xiii. 8. That goodness is no name, and happiness no dream. Byron. Note: In Old England before a vowel the form non or noon… | Nay; not; not at all; not in any respect or degree; -- a word expressing negation, denial, or refusal. Before or after another negative, no is emphatic. We do no otherwise than we are willed. Shak.
nonresistant: One who maintains that no resistance should be made to constituted authority, even when unjustly or oppressively exercised; one who advocates or practices absolute submission; also, one who holds that violence should never be resisted by force.
nothingarian: One of no certain belief; one belonging to no particular sect.
noetical: Of or pertaining to the intellect; intellectual. I would employ the word noetic to express all those cognitions which originate in the mind itself. Sir W. Hamilton.
nortelry: Nurture; education; culture; bringing up. (old) Nortelry . . . learned at the nunnery. Chaucer.
nonconformist: One who does not conform to an established church; especially, one who does not conform to the established church of England; a dissenter.
nonacquiescence: Refusal of acquiescence; failure to yield or comply.
noodle: A simpleton; a blockhead; a stupid person; a ninny. [Low] The chuckling grin of noodles. Sydney Smith. | A thin strip of dough, made with eggs, rolled up, cut into small pieces, and used in soup.
nonproficient: One who has failed to become proficient. NON PROS. Non" pros.` (. An abbreviation of Non prosequitur.
nonane: One of a group of metameric hydrocarbons C9H20 of the paraffin series; -- so called because of the nine carbon atoms in the molecule. Normal nonane is a colorless volatile liquid, an ingredient of ordinary kerosene.
nostrum: 1. A medicine, the ingredients of which are kept secret for the purpose of restricting the profits of sale to the inventor or proprietor; a quack medicine. 2. Any scheme or device proposed by a quack. The incentives of agitators, the arts of impostors and the nostrums of quacks. Brougham.
norther: A wind from the north; esp., a strong and cold north wind in Texas and the vicinity of the Gulf of Mexico.
notepaper: Writing paper, not exceeding in size, when folded once, five by eight inches.
nomenclature: 1. A name. (old) Bacon. 2. A vocabulary, dictionary, or glossary. 3. The technical names used in any particular branch of science or art, or by any school or individual; as, the nomenclature of botany or of chemistry; the nomenclature of Lavoisier and his associates.
nomenclator: 1. One who calls persons or things by their names. Note: In Rome, candidates for office were attended each by a nomenclator, who informed the candidate of the names of the persons whom they met and whose votes it was desirable to solicit. 2. One who gives names to things, or who settles and adjusts the nomenclature of any art or science;
norimon: A Japanese covered litter, carried by men. B. Taylor.
nolition: Adverse action of will; unwillingness; -- opposed to Ant: volition. A nolition and a direct enmity against the lust. Jer. Taylor.
noria: A large water wheel, turned by the action of a stream against its floats, and carrying at its circumference buckets, by which water is raised and discharged into a trough; used in Arabia, China, and elsewhere for irrigating land; a Persian wheel.
nonoxygenous: Without oxygen; characterized by the absence of oxygen; as, a nonoxygenous alkaloid.
nog: 1. A noggin. 2. A kind of strong ale. Halliwell. | 1. A wooden block, of the size of a brick, built into a wall, as a hold for the nails of woodwork. 2. One of the square logs of wood used in a pile to support the roof of a mine. 3.
nocent: 1. Doing hurt, or having a tendency to hurt; hurtful; mischievous; noxious; as, nocent qualities. I. Watts. 2. Guilty; -- the opposite of innocent. (old) Foxe. | A criminal. (old) Sir T. Browne.
nonce: The one or single occasion; the present call or purpose; -- chiefly used in the phrase for the nonce. The miller was a stout carl for the nones. Chaucer. And that he calls for drink, I 'll have prepared him A chalice for the nonce. Shak. Nonce word, "a word apparently employed only for the nonce". Murray (New English Dict. ).
nonslaveholding: Not possessing or holding slaves; as, a nonslaveholding State.
noted: Well known by reputation or report; eminent; celebrated; as, a noted author, or traveler. -- Not"ed*ly, adv. -- Not"ed*ness, n.
notopodium: The dorsal lobe or branch of a parapodium. See Parapodium.
notorious: Generally known and talked of by the public; universally believed to be true; manifest to the world; evident; -- usually in an unfavorable sense; as, a notorious thief; a notorious crime or vice. Your goodness, Since you provoke me, shall be most notorious. Shak. Syn. -- Distinguished; remarkable; conspicuous; celebrated; noted; famous; renowned. -- No*to"ri*ous*ly, adv.
noctivagant: Going about in the night; night-wandering.
nonsane: Unsound; not perfect; as, a person of nonsane memory. Blackstone.
nonintervention: The state or habit of not intervening or interfering; as, the nonintervention of one state in the affairs of another.
novum: A game at dice, properly called novem quinque (L., nine five), the two principal throws being nine and five. (old) Shak.
nodding: Curved so that the apex hangs down; having the top bent downward.
noils: Waste and knots of wool removed by the comb; combings.
nocturne: A night piece, or serenade. The name is now used for a certain graceful and expressive form of instrumental composition, as the nocturne for orchestra in Mendelsohn's "Midsummer-Night's Dream" music.
not: Wot not; know not; knows not. (old) Chaucer. | Shorn; shaven. (old) See Nott.
normanism: A Norman idiom; a custom or expression peculiar to the Normans. M. Arnold.
northwest: The point in the horizon between the north and west, and equally distant from each; the northwest part or region. | 1. Pertaining to, or in the direction of, the point between the north and west; being in the northwest; toward the northwest, or coming from the northwest; as, the northwest coast. 2.
nonresidence: The state or condition of being nonresident, Swift.
nobilitate: To make noble; to ennoble; to exalt. (old)
nostalgic: Of or pertaining to nostalgia; affected with nostalgia.
noncommittal: A state of not being committed or pledged; forbearance or refusal to commit one's self. Also used adjectively.
nostoc: A genus of algæ. The plants are composed of moniliform cells imbedded in a gelatinous substance. Note: Nostoc commune is found on the ground, and is ordinarily not seen; but after a rain it swells up into a conspicuous jellylike mass, whish was formerly supposed to have fallen from the sky, whence the popular names, fallen star and star jelly. Also called witches' butter.
notional: 1. Consisting of, or conveying, notions or ideas; expressing abstract conceptions. 2. Existing in idea only; visionary; whimsical. Discourses of speculative and notional things. Evelyn. 3. Given to foolish or visionary expectations; whimsical; fanciful; as, a notional man.
noonstead: The position of the sun at noon. (old) Drayton.
noy: To annoy; to vex. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.] Piers Plowman. All that noyed his heavy spright. Spenser. | That which annoys. (old) Piers Plowman.
nomopelmous: Having a separate and simple tendon to flex the first toe, or hallux, as do passerine birds.
nostalgia: Homesickness; esp., a severe and sometimes fatal form of melancholia, due to homesickness.
nowadays: In these days; at the present time. What men of spirit, nowadays, Come to give sober judgment of new plays Garrick.
node: 1. A knot, a knob; a protuberance; a swelling. 2. Specifically: (a) (Astron.) One of the two points where the orbit of a planet, or comet, intersects the ecliptic, or the orbit of a satellite intersects the plane of the orbit of its primary. (b) (Bot.) The joint of a stem, or the part where a leaf or several leaves are inserted.
noncompliance: Neglect of compliance; failure to comply.
notaeum: The back or upper surface, as of a bird.
noctograph: 1. A kind of writing frame for the blind. 2. An instrument or register which records the presence of watchmen on their beats. Knight.
nonimporting: Not importing; not bringing from foreign countries.
nonagesimal: Of or pertaining to the ninetieth degree or to a nonagesimal. | The middle or highest point of the part of the ecliptic which is at any given moment above the horizon. It is the ninetieth degree of the ecliptic, reckoned from the points in which it is intersected…
northwardly: Having a northern direction. | In a northern direction.
novatian: One of the sect of Novatius, or Novatianus, who held that the lapsed might not be received again into communion with the church, and that second marriages are unlawful.
nominate: 1. To mention by name; to name. (old) To nominate them all, it is impossible. Shak. 2. To call; to entitle; to denominate. (old) Spenser. 3. To set down in express terms; to state. (old) Is it so noiminated in the bond Shak. 4. To name, or designate by name, for an office or place; to appoint; esp., to name as a candidate for an election, choice, or appointment;
nounal: Of or pertaining to a noun. Verbs which in whole or in part have shed their old nounal coat. Earle.
noddy: 1. A simpleton; a fool. L'Estrange. 2. (Zoöl.) (a) Any tern of the genus Anous, as A. stolidus. (b) The arctic fulmar (Fulmarus glacialis). Sometimes also applied to other sea birds. 3. nonability: 1. Want of ability. 2. (Law) An exception taken against a plaintiff in a cause, when he is unable legally to commence a suit.
notchboard: The board which receives the ends of the steps in a staircase.
noil: A short or waste piece or knot of wool separated from the longer staple by combing; also, a similar piece or shred of waste silk.
nouthe: Just now; at present. (old) But thereof needeth not to speak as nouthe. Chaucer.
noyous: Annoying; disagreeable. (old) Watch the noyous night, and wait for Spenser.
noyade: A drowning of many persons at once, -- a method of execution practiced at Nantes in France during the Reign of Terror, by Jean Baptiste Carrier.
nonexistence: 1. Absence of existence; the negation of being; nonentity. A. Baxter. 2. A thing that has no existence. Sir T. Browne.
nomination: 1. The act of naming or nominating; designation of a person as a candidate for office; the power of nominating; the state of being nominated. notionally: In mental apprehension; in conception; not in reality. Two faculties . . . notionally or really distinct. Norris.
noggin: 1. A small mug or cup. 2. A measure equivalent to a gill. [Prov. Eng.]
norseman: One of the ancient Scandinavians; a Northman.
nominatival: Of or pertaining to the nominative case.
nonexportation: A failure of exportation; a not exporting of commodities.
norn: 1. (Scandinavian Myth.) One of the three Fates, Past, Present, and Future. Their names were Urd, Verdandi, and Skuld. 2. A tutelary deity; a genius.
noblesse: 1. Dignity; greatness; noble birth or condition. (old) Chaucer. Spenser. B. Jonson. 2. The nobility; persons of noble rank collectively, including males and females. Dryden.
noncomposmentis: Not of sound mind; not having the regular use of reason; hence, also, as a noun, an idiot; a lunati NONCON. Non"con. (, n. See Noncontent.
nontronite: A greenish yellow or green mineral, consisting chiefly of the hydrous silicate of iron.
nonfeasance: An omission or neglect to do something, esp. that which ought to have been done. Cf. Malfeasance.
northman: One of the inhabitants of the north of Europe; esp., one of the ancient Scandinavians; a Norseman.
nozzle: 1. The nose; the snout; hence, the projecting vent of anything; as, the nozzle of a bellows. 2. Specifically: (a) A short tube, usually tapering, forming the vent of a hose or pipe. (b) A short outlet, or inlet, pipe projecting from the end or side of a hollow vessel, as a steam-engine cylinder or a steam boiler.
noncommissioned: Not having a commission. Noncommissioned officer (Mil.), a subordinate officer not appointed by a commission from the chief executive or supreme authority of the State; but by the Secretary of War or by the commanding officer of the regiment.
nonresistance: The principles or practice of a nonresistant; passive obedience; submission to authority, power, oppression, or violence without opposition.
nonappointment: Neglect of making appointment; failure to receive an appointment.
nosing: That part of the treadboard of a stair which projects over the riser; hence, any like projection, as the projecting edge of a molding.
notochordal: Of or pertaining to the notochord; having a notochord.
nonconcur: To dissent or refuse to concur.
nominally: In a nominal manner; by name; in name only; not in reality. Burke.
northeastern: Of or pertaining to the northeast; northeasterly.
nominatively: In the manner of a nominative; as a nominative.
novice: 1. One who is new in any business, profession, or calling; one unacquainted or unskilled; one yet in the rudiments; a beginner; a tyro. I am young; a novice in the trade. Dryden. 2. | Like a novice; becoming a novice. (old)
northwesterly: Toward the northwest, or from the northwest.
nonuser: 1. A not using; failure to use. An office may be forfeited by misuser or nonuser. Blackstone. 2. (Law) Neglect or omission to use an easement or franchise or to assert a right. Kent.
nogging: Rough brick masonry used to fill in the interstices of a wooden frame, in building.
nocake: Indian corn parched, and beaten to powder, -- used for food by the Northern American Indians.
now: 1. At the present time; at this moment; at the time of speaking; instantly; as, I will write now. I have a patient now living, at an advanced age, who discharged blood from his lungs thirty years… | Existing at the present time; present. "Our now happiness." Glanvill.
nonsequitur: An inference which does not follow from the premises.
note: To butt; to push with the horns. [Prov. Eng.] | Need; needful business. (old) Chaucer.
nomarch: The chief magistrate of a nome or nomarchy.
novitious: Newly invented; recent; new. (old) Bp. Pearson.
nocturn: 1. An office of devotion, or act of religious service, by night. 2. One of the portions into which the Psalter was divided, each consisting of nine psalms, designed to be used at a night service. Hook.
noviceship: The state of being a novice; novitiate.
norfolkspaniel: One of a breed of field spaniels similar to the clumbers, but shorter in body and of a liver-and-white or black-and-white color.
noggen: Made of hemp; hence, hard; rough; harsh. (old) Johnson.
nonnitrognous: Devoid of nitrogen; as, a nonnitrogenous principle; a nonnitrogenous food. See the Note under Food, n., 1.
novel: Of recent origin or introduction; not ancient; new; hence, out of the ordinary course; unusual; strange; surprising. Note: In civil law, the novel or new constitutions are those which are… | 1. That which is new or unusual; a novelty. 2. pl. News; fresh tidings. (old) Some came of curiosity to hear some novels. Latimer. 3. A fictitious tale or narrative, professing to be conformed to…
northing: 1. (Surv. & Navigation) Distance northward from any point of departure or of reckoning, measured on a meridian; -- opposed to Ant: southing. 2. (Astron.) The distance of any heavenly body from the equator northward; north declination.
nomology: 1. The science of law; legislation. 2. The science of the laws of the mind; rational psychology. Sir W. Hamilton.
nonconformity: Neglect or failure of conformity; especially, in England, the neglect or refusal to unite with the established church in its rites and modes of worship.
notoriety: The quality or condition of being notorious; the state of being generally or publicly known; -- commonly used in an unfavorable sense; as, the notoriety of a crime. They were not subjects in their own nature so exposed to public notoriety. Addison.
nomenclatural: Pertaining or according to a nomenclature.
notorhizal: Having the radicle of the embryo lying against the back of one of the cotyledons; incumbent.
nonexecution: Neglect or failure of execution; nonperformance.
nondescript: Not hitherto described; novel; hence, odd; abnormal; unclassifiable. | A thing not yet described; that of which no account or explanation has been given; something abnormal, or hardly classifiable.
noninflectional: Not admitting of, or characterized by, inflection.
nobody: 1. No person; no one; not anybody. 2. Hence: A person of no influence or importance; an insignificant or contemptible person. [Colloq.]
norma: 1. A norm; a principle or rule; a model; a standard. J. S. Mill. 2. A mason's or a carpenter's square or rule. 3. A templet or gauge.
nosed: Having a nose, or such a nose; -- chieflay used in composition; as, pug-nosed.
noisy: 1. Making a noise, esp. a loud sound; clamorous; vociferous; turbulent; boisterous; as, the noisy crowd. 2. Full of noise. "The noisy town." Dryden.
